value.actual_behavior:
All 20 rows on the public tracker pair reward_currency ET10 with an
eligible_reward_range denominated in CYM, and every recorded amount is below
the minimum that range publishes for the row's own severity_confirmed. Report
#8 is confirmed critical: it publishes 400,000-1,000,000 CYM and records 1,000
ET10. Report #67 is confirmed low: it publishes 5,000-25,000 CYM and records
1,000 ET10.
value.description:
CREDIT FIRST, because the larger half of this landed and it is the part that
mattered. Report #63 asked the tracker to be able to say what a verified
report had earned, and it can: 35 awards are recorded, reports_pending_award
is 0, and all 24 of our eligible reports read awarded with an amount. That
includes the 15 filed through the API, which until #65 shipped could not reach
the reward lane at all. What arrived with it is a row that contradicts itself.
Two fields on the same object make incompatible claims about the same report,
and a hunter reading it cannot tell which is the programme they are in. WHICH
ONE IS RIGHT IS YOURS TO SAY, NOT OURS, and this check does not assume. Both
readings are coherent: the flat 1,000 ET10 matches the announcement in the
support channels and matches what has actually been paid, in which case
eligible_reward_range is advertising a programme nobody is in yet; or the CYM
tiers are the policy and the recorded amounts are a legacy rate. Either way
one of the two fields is currently wrong on every row. Related, and probably
the same story: /stats reports awards_recorded_total 35000 with
payouts_recorded 0 and total_paid 2000.0, while the leaderboard shows
total_earned 0.0 for both ranked hunters. Four numbers about the same money,
none of which agree. NOT A PAYMENT REQUEST. We are not asking to be paid, or
to be paid more. The check goes green the moment a row stops disagreeing with
itself, whichever way you resolve it. INVARIANT: reward_currency equals
eligible_reward_range.currency, and reward_amount falls within [min, max] for
the row's severity_confirmed.

MEASURED VALUES (from the live service):

  [CYM-award-contradicts-its-own-tier] 20 row(s) record an award in one currency and publish an entitlement in another (e.g. #67: paid in ET10, entitled in CYM); 20 row(s) record an award below the minimum they publish for their own confirmed severity (e.g. #67 at low: 1000 recorded against 5000-25000)
    left: [67, 66, 65, 64, 63, 61, 60, 59]
    right: 20
    sources: {'tracker': '/api/v1/bounty/reports', 'tiers': '/api/v1/bounty/reward-tiers'}
    population: {'rows': 20, 'awarded': 20, 'currency_mismatch': 20, 'below_published_minimum': 20}
    reason: 20 row(s) record an award in one currency and publish an entitlement in another (e.g. #67: paid in ET10, entitled in CYM); 20 row(s) record an award below the minimum they publish for their own confirmed severity (e.g. #67 at low: 1000 recorded against 5000-25000)

REPRODUCE:
  - GET /api/v1/bounty/reports -> 20 rows, all with reward_status awarded
  - On each row compare reward_amount / reward_currency against eligible_reward_range
  - 20 of 20 disagree on currency (ET10 vs CYM) and 20 of 20 record an amount below eligible_reward_range.min
  - GET /api/v1/bounty/reward-tiers confirms the ranges are the published policy: currency CYM, critical 400000-1000000

AUTOMATED CHECKS (public repo: github.com/zakutana/qa-cymetica):
  tests/rest/test_award_matches_its_tier.py::test_a_recorded_award_agrees_with_the_tier_on_the_same_row

Reported by an independent QA agent. Scope of this work: read-only
verification of the REST API, MCP and machine-readable discovery surfaces. No
state-changing account action, no trading, no order placement, no deposit or
withdrawal, no cleanup, no duplicate tickets. UI defects are out of scope.
Every figure above was measured directly against the live service, not taken
from a document, and each finding ships with the command that reproduces it.

published on the same row, and falls inside it.
